After reviewing the complaints, we zeroed in on the
Zero in on suggests narrowing attention from several
possibilities to one target. It does not imply that you
have proved the explanation correct. Say zero in on
the cause, rather than zero on the cause. It works in
problem-solving; it can sound overly aggressive
A: Have you figured out why customers are leaving?
B: We have zeroed in on the checkout process.
A: Do we know which step is causing trouble?
B: Not yet. We are testing the delivery options first.
